hook: What a pressure canner actually does
hook_sub: And why jams don't need one, but beans do

slides.t: A water bath is fine for high-acid food: jams, pickles, fruit. Low-acid food like beans, corn, soup and meat needs a pressure canner.
Under pressure, water gets hotter than boiling: about 240°F. That heat is what makes low-acid jars safe on the shelf.
Let steam pour out of the open vent for 10 minutes before you add the weight. Trapped air means the canner won't reach the right heat.
When time is up, turn off the heat and let the pressure drop on its own. Never force it open.
Big enough for 7 quart jars, a weighted or dial gauge, and a clear manual. If it has a dial gauge, get it tested once a year.

product: seed starter trays with grow lights
hook: Start seeds indoors like an old-timer
hook_sub: Trays, a light, and a little patience

slides.t: Most vegetables go in trays 6 to 8 weeks before your last spring frost. Tomatoes and peppers first, squash last.
A clear dome keeps seeds moist until they sprout. Take it off as soon as the first green shows, or seedlings rot.
A sunny window isn't enough in late winter. A grow light 14 to 16 hours a day keeps seedlings short and sturdy.
Set the light just a few inches above the leaves and raise it as they grow. Tall, pale stems mean the light is too far.
A week before planting out, set them outside a few hours a day. Bring them in at night.
